acceptance: Before anything is sent the compute dock names PuppyOne compute and shows no prompt, picker, balance or account detail, and nothing is read, saved, selected or opened.

Every ready configured model is offered in Chat's model picker and a choice is reported, not configured, in Chat; a ready own route restores as ready with its source; connection management stays in Settings.
While a turn runs the model choice is disabled and a disabled picker never opens or chooses.

A new connections catalog makes the chat rediscover its runtime once (the same catalog does not); signing in, the user's own model and the balance are handed to the account and Settings without selecting a model or sending a turn.
A signed-in account whose compute is loading, or ready but still awaiting its model, shows a disabled Connecting to compute action instead of a billing error, and the route is not ready.

An empty balance blocks a selected PuppyOne model with 'Add credit to use this model.' and a Manage AI balance action that opens the account and never checks out; with credit PuppyOne compute offers no model choice and is ready exactly when a model is selected.

reason: Chat's compute snapshot (`read_compute_snapshot`) only knows signed out, no credit and ready: it has no managed-compute failure code (gateway unavailable), no Retry that refreshes with progress (the dock's Retry only rereads, and its 'temporarily unavailable' state is unreachable), no in-Chat browser sign-in handoff whose failure could be labelled (sign-in goes to the account), and no server-configured trial credit line (`agent.compute.trialGranted`, `signInUnavailable` are unused).

acceptance: The composer's only configuration is the session's own controls: a Model when the session has one (never an Agent or backend control), nothing when it has none, and the input and its single action stay; a chat without a selected runtime offers no models and cannot send.
The runtime catalog keeps registry order and products without provider-specific filtering; enabled lists keep only installed enabled Agents and visible lists drop hidden and uninstalled ones.
Choosing a model by pointer reports it, closes the picker and the trigger shows the new label; a large catalog shows at most 120 options with a 'Showing 120 of N' note and search narrows it.

reason: TS keeps AgentRuntimePicker and AgentSurfaceHeader only for its visual smoke harness; the product chooses the Agent on the launcher before a chat mounts and the chat has no Agent picker (contract agent-launcher-before-chat). The native app has no in-chat runtime picker or surface header, so its flat menu, warnings and focus return have no counterpart.

acceptance: Local Agents settings list the detected Agents (not the Built-in Agent) under Active Chat, Chat History and Hooks; hiding an Agent persists only its id and the history switch only its flag; every detected configurable Hook starts off and discovery never enrolls; Hooks install one provider at a time and turn on file activity.
